top_choice_rationale: P002 (B012: Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) recognises the origination of nominal-rigidity mechanisms and their integration into a microfounded framework for monetary policy. These are three separable contributions to a framework that is 25 to 45 years old. It has been modified, not refuted, by 2008 and 2021-23, and no earlier prize has covered it directly. I rank it first on achievement, maturity and scope, and I accept its weaker attribution. Eight names are credited, any three-name cut is a judgement call, and the Taylor rule alone is thin. The micro evidence on state-dependent pricing qualifies Calvo's time-dependent assumption without removing his origination role. P001 (B026: Melitz, Helpman) is a close second. It has cleaner attribution and more direct repeated firm-level confirmation, but a narrower scope, and Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are uncredited. P003 (B007: Kiyotaki, Moore) is a clean two-author mechanism, but it is narrower, its empirical identification is weaker, and the 2022 prize is adjacent. All three are defensible awards, so I place no award last. I do not treat support counts as merit.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Melitz, Helpman, Kiyotaki or Moore. My field of market and mechanism design is not a field of any ranked candidate.
